messages:
Maya (support): FYI — customer Eli from Acme Health reporting frequent AI streaming failures. They see a ton of 5xx spikes in their dashboard tied to streaming responses. Says it started after they rolled an http client lib update last week.

Eli (customer): hitting /v1/stream/chat with long-lived SSEs. often gets partial responses then connection drops. logs show `write: broken pipe` on client side and our gateway emits 502/503, which then counts as 5xx in billing/alerts.

Maya (support): Pasted the minimal repro they gave below (they say curl reproduces ~30% of streams failing after ~45s):

```
# repro (customer):
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-xxl","stream":true,"prompt":"long stream..."}' \
  "https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/stream/chat"
```

Eli (customer): note they use an HTTP/2-capable client behind corporate proxy. When they force `--http1.1` behavior failures drop to ~2%.

Kyle (sre): Thanks. Two things to check: 1) how our gateway interprets client disconnects (EPIPE/ECONNRESET) for streaming endpoints, 2) chunked encoding / http2 flow control interplay causing our proxy to terminate upstream.

Anita (eng-runtime): I pulled matching logs for X-Request-ID from their repro. Upstream model backend is still streaming tokens, then gateway logs show `upstream prematurely closed connection` and we emit 502 to client. Backend shows no error. Gateway log snippet: 

```
[2026-03-14T16:12:13Z] req=xyz123 method=POST path=/v1/stream/chat upstream=10.2.3.11:8080 status=502 msg="upstream prematurely closed connection" bytes_sent=1420
[2026-03-14T16:12:13Z] backend=runner-04 pid=1342 action=stream-send result=ok until=16:12:12.984
```

Maya (support): The billing/alerts are picking those up as hard 5xx, not the 499/4xx client-closed codes. Customer is worried about being charged and about alarms.

Kyle (sre): It looks like our edge (envoy/nginx hybrid) is interpreting the socket write error as an upstream failure because the client closed while we were still writing a chunk; we then retry-to-fallback which converts to a 5xx in our metric pipeline. We should avoid retry/fallback for streaming endpoints.

Anita (eng-runtime): Agreed. Two immediate mitigations: 
- Mark streaming endpoints in the gateway config so client disconnects map to 499-like counters and do NOT trigger backend retries.
- Add a small graceful shutdown window where we swallow EPIPE/EINTR while finishing chunk writes, and ensure proxy doesn't convert them to 5xx.

Kyle (sre): Quick diagnostic steps for Support/Customer: ask them to run two repros and capture headers and tcpdump. Steps: 
1) run `curl -v --http1.1 -N ...` and save verbose output
2) run `curl -v --http2 -N ...` (or their default)
3) capture the response-chunk boundaries (we want to see `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` and any `CONTENT-LENGTH` mismatch)
4) if possible capture `strace`/`tcpdump` to show `RST` or `FIN` from client side.

Eli (customer): I can do that. Attaching their sample verbose run: `state: client sent FIN at ~45s; server still streaming`.

Maya (support): I added these as steps and asked for request-id and curl output. Also temporarily disabled customer-level retry in their account to avoid double charging/duplicate requests.

Anita (eng-runtime): Internal followups: 
- I opened an internal issue: ENG-STREAM-1429 to mark streaming endpoints in service discovery metadata (so gateway knows semantics).
- We'll add an envoy filter to map ECONNRESET/EPIPE during outgoing write to a 499 metric and suppress retry.
- Also verifying HTTP/2 WINDOW updates: if client uses HTTP/2 and stops consuming, connection can end up with upstream blocking and gateway treats as upstream failure.

Kyle (sre): For monitoring: emit two separate counters for streaming endpoint failures: `stream.client_disconnect` and `stream.upstream_abort`. Right now metric `http.5xx` conflates both. That will stop paging ops for client-caused disconnects.

Anita (eng-runtime): Patch candidate (config snippet for gateway):
```
# envoy filter pseudo
- name: filter.stream-client-disconnect
  match: { path_prefix: "/v1/stream" }
  on_client_disconnect: report_as: client_disconnect
  suppress_retries: true
```

Maya (support): ETA on fix? Customer needs short-term workaround.

Anita (eng-runtime): I can land the metric separation + suppress_retries flag in config in ~2 working days, and envoy filter testing + canary in 4 days. If customer can switch to HTTP/1.1 as temporary workaround that'll reduce the likelihood of the failure.

Kyle (sre): Also adding a quick rule in the routing layer to treat `write: broken pipe` logs coming from the edge as non-5xx for the next 48h to avoid noisy alerts while we deploy the proper fix. I'll coordinate with ops to whitelist the request-ids for backfill.

Eli (customer): thanks — we'll try forcing http1.1 and send tcpdump. Appreciate the disable of retries for our account.

Maya (support): Closing loop: I've created support ticket SUP-3765 with full repro steps and linked ENG-STREAM-1429. Leaving open until eng confirms canary. :thumbsup:

alerts-bot: [alert suppressed] stream-5xx-surge for customer=acme-health (now count mapped to client_disconnect)

Anita (eng-runtime): leaving notes in ENG-STREAM-1429: ensure streaming request metadata includes `streaming=true`, wire level detection for `Transfer-Encoding: chunked`, and a map of socket errors->metrics.

Kyle (sre): followup action items: 1) dev deploy feature flag to suppress retries for streaming endpoints, 2) metric update to split disconnects, 3) docs update for Support with repro checklist.

Maya (support): I'll update the customer ticket with these mitigations and expected timeline. If they can share tcpdump, we'll attach to the eng issue.

-- end of thread --
